graph.canvasLabel: Screen-reader label of the graph canvas. {count} is the number of cards drawn. Escape is the keyboard key; keep the key name as is.
graph.search.placeholder: Placeholder of the search box floating over the graph. 'Nodes' are the cards drawn as boxes.
graph.control.fit: Tooltip and screen-reader label of an icon button (⤢) that zooms so the whole graph fits the screen.
graph.control.reset: Tooltip of an icon button (⟲) that resets the camera. One short word.
graph.control.resetLabel: Screen-reader label of the same reset button (⟲): resets the camera position and zoom.
graph.panel.open: Link in the small pill shown under a selected card; opens the card's page. Keep the arrow. Short — the pill is one line.
graph.tabs.group: Screen-reader label of the two-button switch between the Graph and Atlas readings of the plan.
graph.tabs.graph.label: Segmented button, top-left over the canvas: the force-directed node graph. One short word.
graph.tabs.atlas.label: Segmented button, top-left over the canvas: the plan drawn as an isometric city (atlas = a book of maps). One short word.
graph.tabs.atlas.hint: Tooltip of the Atlas button. 'Isometric' is the 3D drawing style.
atlas.canvasLabel: Screen-reader label of the atlas canvas. {count} is the number of cards, each drawn as a building in a city.
atlas.lens.label: Small uppercase label before the lens dropdown. A lens is the question the map answers (height and colour of buildings).
atlas.lens.status.label: Lens option in a dropdown about 10rem wide: colour buildings by card status.
atlas.lens.status.hint: Explanation shown next to the dropdown when this lens is picked. The colon followed by a dash is intentional in English; a legend sits there.
atlas.lens.degree.label: Lens option: building height by number of connections. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.degree.hint: Hubs = cards with many connections; towers = tall buildings.
atlas.lens.drift.label: Lens option: show cards whose code changed since the card was last verified ('drift'). Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.drift.hint: 'Bound code' = source files linked to the card. 'Scaffolded' = drawn with a scaffolding cage, meaning drifted.
atlas.lens.recency.label: Lens option: building height by how recently the card was edited. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.size.label: Lens option: building height by lines of code. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.size.hint: FILE is a card type name; keep it as is.
atlas.engine.group: Screen-reader label of the two-button switch for how the city is drawn (flat 2D shading vs 3D).
atlas.engine.flat.label: Small segmented button, top-right: draw the city with flat 2D shading. One short word.
atlas.engine.flat.title: Tooltip of the Flat button.
atlas.engine.lit.label: Small segmented button, top-right: draw the city in lit 3D. Keep it as short as '3D'.
atlas.engine.lit.title: Tooltip of the 3D button.
atlas.control.fit: Screen-reader label of an icon button (⤢) that zooms out so the whole city fits.
atlas.control.export: Screen-reader label of an icon button (⤓) that saves the map as an image.
atlas.inside.back: Button in a small chip, shown after clicking into a building; returns to the whole city. Keep the arrow.
atlas.legend: One-line keyboard and mouse hint along the bottom edge of the map, shown in uppercase. → and ← are the arrow keys. Keep it short; it truncates.
atlas.readout.parts: Hover readout for a building. {count} is how many parts (files, functions or sections) it has; {names} is a list of the first few part names (plan data).
atlas.readout.partsMore: Same as atlas.readout.parts, but the card has more than three parts and only three are named, so the list ends with an ellipsis.
atlas.readout.drifted: Hover readout for a building whose linked code changed since the card was verified.
atlas.readout.driftedWithParts: Same as atlas.readout.drifted, followed by {parts} = the text of atlas.readout.parts.
atlas.trace.region: Screen-reader label of the panel that walks through a FLOW card step by step on the map.
atlas.trace.close: Screen-reader label of the ✕ button that closes the flow-trace panel.
atlas.trace.play: Button that auto-advances through the flow's steps. Small button; keep short.
atlas.trace.pause: Same button while playing; stops auto-advance. Keep short.
atlas.trace.step: Step counter, e.g. '3/7'. {step} is the current step number, {total} the number of steps.
atlas.trace.at: Shown at the right of the trace controls: the building (card) the current step happens at. {handle} is a card id like API-TICKETS, drawn as a chip.
